For \(k\ge 2\), we have \(a_k=k^{a_{k-1}}\). Modulo \(k+1\),

\[
a_k \equiv (-1)^{a_{k-1}}.
\]

Since \(k+1\ge 3\), this is \(1\) iff \(a_{k-1}\) is even.

Now for \(n\ge 2\),

\[
a_n=n^{a_{n-1}},
\]

so \(a_n\) has the same parity as \(n\). Also \(a_1=1\) is odd. Hence \(a_{k-1}\) is even iff \(k-1\ge 2\) and \(k-1\) is even, i.e. \(k\ge 3\) and \(k\) is odd.

Thus we count odd integers \(k\) from \(3\) to \(2020\):

\[
\frac{2019-3}{2}+1=1009.
\]

\[
\boxed{1009}
\]
